recommendation_1: Reduce the hidden dimension in the first fully connected layer from 128 to 32 to significantly decrease the number of trainable parameters and memory footprint.
rationale_1: The current architecture uses 128 hidden units which increases computational overhead and memory usage. Reducing to 32 maintains model capacity while drastically cutting down resource requirements for both training and inference in a federated setting.
recommendation_3: Use Bfloat16 Autocast for CPU execution during training and inference to reduce memory usage and increase throughput without sacrificing model performance.
rationale_3: BF16 offers a good balance between precision and efficiency compared to FP32, allowing for faster computations and lower memory consumption on CPUs, particularly beneficial when running on low-power devices.
recommendation_4: Implement L1 Unstructured Pruning on the weights of the first fully connected layer with a pruning ratio of 0.4 to remove redundant connections and further compress the model.
rationale_4: Pruning removes unnecessary parameters without retraining the entire model, reducing both memory footprint and computational cost. Applying it to the most significant layer (fc1) maximizes compression benefits while preserving functionality.
recommendation_5: Replace ReLU activation with Swish (SiLU) function after the first linear layer to improve gradient flow and reduce training time, but ensure proper integration with other optimizations.
rationale_5: While Swish can improve convergence speed, it should be used carefully as seen in experiments where it caused instability. Combining it with pruning and quantization will help maintain stability and further enhance efficiency.
recommendation_6: Remove dropout regularization since it adds overhead without significant gain in this simple classification task and may hinder convergence under strict resource constraints.
rationale_6: Dropout introduces additional computation during training and requires extra memory for storing intermediate activations. Removing it simplifies the model and aligns better with green AI principles for resource-constrained environments.
